Integral Symbol

There is no legacy Windows Alt code for Integral because it is not in either the OEM code page 437 or Windows-1252 tables. The Unicode codepoint is U+222B, which you can use as ∫ in HTML, \222B in CSS, or type with Alt+8747 on Windows (BMP only). If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, use the Character Viewer, the HTML entity, or copy the character directly. Integral is outside both legacy code pages, which is why U+222B is the identifier that works across Word, HTML, CSS, Python and JavaScript. HTML also defines the named entity ∫ for Integral, but the numeric form ∫ is safer when compatibility is uncertain.

How to type integral on Windows

  1. Turn Num Lock on so the numeric keypad is active.
  2. Hold the left Alt key.
  3. Type 8 7 4 7 on the numeric keypad for the decimal codepoint 8747.
  4. Release Alt. The Integral character (∫) appears.

If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, see how to type symbols without a numpad.

How to type integral on macOS

There is no direct Option shortcut for Integral. Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space, search for "Integral" and click the character to insert it.

How to use integral in code

  • HTML: or , also
  • CSS: content:"\222B"; ()
  • Python: \u222B or chr(0x222B)
  • JavaScript: \u222B or String.fromCodePoint(0x222B)
  • JSON: "\u222B"
  • LaTeX: $\int$ (math mode)

Frequently asked questions

Is there an Alt code for ∫?

No legacy Alt code exists for Integral because it is not in code page 437 or Windows-1252. Use the Unicode codepoint U+222B in HTML, CSS or the Character Viewer instead.

How do I type ∫ without a numpad?

Use the Windows Character Viewer (Win+.), the macOS Character Viewer (⌃⌘Space), an HTML entity such as ∫, or copy the character directly from this page.

Why does Alt+8747 not work?

Alt+8747 only works on a keyboard with a physical numeric keypad. It also requires the application to accept the numeric-keypad input path. Laptops without a numpad need an alternative method.

What is the Unicode for Integral?

The Unicode codepoint for Integral is U+222B. You can use this value in HTML as ∫, in CSS as \222B, and in Word with Alt+X.

How do I type ∫ on a Mac?

Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space and search for the character name or U+222B, then click it.
